name: Ze-Yu Xing
institution: Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
bio:
My research explores novel phenomena in quantum systems far from equilibrium, with a current focus on open quantum systems and quantum many-body dynamics. I seek to understand how collective behavior emerges and what general principles govern dynamics and relaxation. My earlier work on non-Hermitian physics forms part of this broader interest in quantum behavior beyond equilibrium.

More broadly, I am curious about how concepts from information theory and probability can deepen our understanding of physical systems. Looking ahead, I aim to explore connections between fundamental theoretical physics and advances in artificial intelligence: how AI can help us investigate complex quantum systems and discover new phenomena, and how insights from physics and information theory might inform new approaches to learning and computation. Through these connections, I hope to contribute both to fundamental understanding and to technologies such as quantum computing and AI.
